items.title: 52222_Marshall Royal oral history interview
items.q: I worked for about a week with a little band down at the Downbeat down on Central Avenue, with Lee Young's orchestra.

ctx.x: And Eddie Haywood, you worked with (inaudible)?

Eddie Haywood, I worked with him. That was my -- when I first got out of service, the ending of 1945, I came back in town and I worked for about a week with a little band down at the Downbeat down on Central Avenue, with Lee Young's orchestra. It was a good little swing thing down there. We had three horns and a rhythm section and we worked in a little joint called the Downbeat. Kay Star's (PHONETIC) husband owned

items.title: 53279_Lee Young Oral History Interview
items.q: I had John Simmons, Gerald Wiggins, Maxwell Davis, and Marshall Royal was playing in this band with me.

ctx.x: The Casbah, that's the name of it, right -- out on Figaro4. Well, with the Casbah, let's see ... I think that was the band where I had -- this was when Les Brown and his band used to come to hear my band play, because we were playing things like "I Got My Love to Keep Me Warm", you know, that hit thing they had, and we were playing Dizzy's "Manteca" and I think at this time, it seems to me that I had John Simmons, Gerald Wiggins, Maxwell Davis, and Marshall Royal was playing in this band with me. And Henry Coker…

And we would play all the big band arrangements, and so all the bands would come and hear us, because I was a stickler for 7 pieces, because you could always get the big band sound out of 7 pieces, if it's voiced correctly.
